headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,180 AHEAD OF THURSDAY PCE — SOFT PRINT BELOW 3.4% COULD TRIGGER $4,400; HOT PRINT EXTENDS CORRECTION TO $3,850
snippet: With gold stabilizing near $4,180 after recovering from its June 23 close of $4,129 — a 26% drawdown from January's $5,589 all-time high — GoldSilver.com's June 24 analysis maps the binary setup into Thursday's May PCE release (the Fed's preferred inflation gauge): a soft reading below 3.4% would sharply reprice the 89%-probability December rate hike currently priced into fed funds futures, opening a path back toward $4,400; a hot reading at or above the Fed's 3.6% year-end forecast extends the correction and validates Deutsche Bank and BofA's September hike calls. Nine of nineteen FOMC members at Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's June meeting projected at least one additional 2026 rate increase — the same hawkish configuration that drove gold from $5,589 to $4,129 in six months — but the east-west demand divergence (China +76% YoY gold imports, central banks on pace for 650+ tonnes) provides structural support that was absent during the 2012–2014 bear market, making Thursday morning's data release the single most important event for junior gold miners' share prices this week.

headline: HAMILTON: GDXJ'S BEST QUARTER IN HISTORY — CASH FLOWS BLAST 138% HIGHER TO $7.17B, P/E HITS 40-QUARTER LOW OF 16.9X
snippet: Adam Hamilton's definitive June 24 quarterly analysis of GDXJ's top 25 mid-tier gold miners confirms Q1 2026 as the best earnings quarter in the sector's history by a wide margin: cash flows generated from operations surged 137.9% year-over-year to $7.17 billion as the quarterly average gold price reached $4,873 per ounce (up 70% YoY), while cash and equivalents on balance sheets hit a record $17.75 billion — up 65.5% YoY — giving mid-tiers financial firepower for exploration, M&A, and dividends at levels never seen before. All-in sustaining costs averaged $1,844 per ounce (record high, but royalty-driven and rising far slower than gold), and the GDXJ top 25's trailing twelve-month price-to-earnings ratio has compressed to just 16.9x — the lowest valuation recorded across 40 consecutive quarters of Hamilton's tracking — meaning mid-tier gold producers generating 60% operating margins are currently priced as cheaply relative to earnings as at any point in the four-year run from $1,800 to $5,589. Hamilton flags the June 2026 correction as the most disproportionate compression of miner valuations versus spot gold in the current cycle, creating the same setup that preceded every major GDXJ rally phase since Q3 2024.

headline: G50 CORP WHITE CAPS NEVADA: FIRST 2026 CORE HOLE DRILLS 13.5m AT 7.67 g/t AU FROM 304m — CARLIN LIMESTONE DELIVERS
snippet: G50 Corp (ASX:G50) announced June 22 that the first core hole of its 2026 drill program at the White Caps Gold Project in Lander County, Nevada intersected 13.5 metres at 7.67 g/t gold and 2.38 g/t silver from 304.5 metres depth — including a 3.93-metre high-grade core at 23.95 g/t Au and 7.29 g/t Ag from 305.5 metres — validating Carlin-style gold mineralization in decalcified and silicified limestone at the site of historical underground workings that previously reached 400 metres depth. The 2025 reverse-circulation program had already confirmed 3.5% antimony (35,000 ppm) at shallow depths at White Caps — a US-designated critical mineral — and the 2026 core program (five holes, 2,220 metres total) was designed to establish the depth extension and grade continuity of the Carlin-style system below the historical workings; with hole WC26-001 hitting economic grades at the first attempt, all five holes are now complete and assay results for holes 2 through 5 will determine whether this becomes a resource-definition target in 2026.

headline: SILVERCORP GC MINE: 18.3Mt AT 65 g/t SILVER IN CHINA — RESERVES UP 25% IN TONNES AS UPDATED 43-101 VALIDATES DEPTH EXTENSIONS
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Silvercorp Metals Inc. (TSX:SVM)
snippet: Silvercorp Metals Inc. (TSX:SVM) released June 23 an updated NI 43-101 Technical Report on its Gaocheng Silver-Lead-Zinc (GC) Mine in Guangdong Province, China — prepared by SRK Consulting China Ltd with an effective date of December 31, 2025 — confirming Measured and Indicated Mineral Resources of 18.3 million tonnes grading 65 g/t silver, 0.91% lead, and 2.24% zinc, containing 38.3 million ounces of silver, 167,000 tonnes of lead, and 408,000 tonnes of zinc, with the total Proven plus Probable GC Mine Mineral Reserve tonnes increasing 25% compared to the prior June 2024 technical report. Silvercorp currently operates both the high-grade Ying Mining District (Henan Province, primary asset, recently updated to 50% reserve increase in tonnes) and the GC Mine in a portfolio configuration that makes it one of the few TSX-listed primary silver producers operating entirely at cashflow-positive margins at current silver prices near $65-67 per ounce, and the GC Mine reserve increase validates the underground development that was completed in fiscal 2025 and positions the mine for expanded throughput in fiscal 2027.

headline: DISCOVERY SILVER IS DEAD — DISCOVERY MINING BORN AS 99.6% OF SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE REBRAND REFLECTING GOLD/CU/ZN IDENTITY
snippet: Discovery Silver Corp. shareholders voted 99.6% in favour at the June 22 Annual General and Special Meeting to change the company's name to Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX:DSV), reflecting the company's transformation from a pure silver developer into a growing gold producer with a multi-metal profile that now includes copper, zinc, and silver alongside gold — the new name acknowledges that gold and base metals have become the primary drivers of near-term cashflow while the Cordero silver project in Chihuahua, Mexico (one of the world's largest undeveloped silver deposits, with a globally significant measured and indicated silver resource) continues to advance on its own development timeline. The rebrand is significant for retail investors tracking the silver sector: it signals that even Cordero's owner believes the current period favours production-oriented gold and base metal identity over developer-stage silver positioning, and that Discovery's management team is building a production narrative rather than waiting for a silver price recovery to drive Cordero's development economics.

headline: NIOBAY KICKS OFF SUMMER NIOBIUM SEASON — CREVIER DRILL STARTS IN QUEBEC, JAMES BAY GEOPHYSICS UNDERWAY IN ONTARIO
snippet: NioBay Metals Inc. (TSXV:NBY) announced June 23 that its summer 2026 exploration campaign has commenced across both flagship assets: diamond drilling has begun at the Crevier Property approximately 50 kilometres north of Girardville, Quebec — 150 km from the operating Niobec mine — with geological supervision by IOS Geoscientific Services and drilling by Mashteuiatsh First Nations Drilling; simultaneously, an inspection and geophysical survey program has launched at the James Bay Niobium Project approximately 42 kilometres south of Moose Factory, Ontario, with an airborne survey planned for later in the season. The 2026 campaign builds on the February 25, 2026 updated mineral resource estimate and targets the structural controls on high-grade niobium (Nb2O5) mineralization at Crevier that were identified in 2025 — niobium's growing role in high-strength steel for automotive lightweighting and increasingly as a battery anode material in lithium-niobium oxide configurations positions Crevier as one of the strategically relevant North American niobium projects at a time when China controls over 80% of global niobium refining.

headline: CONTANGO MOBILIZES 2 HELI-RIGS AT LUCKY SHOT — 6,800m ALASKA SURFACE PROGRAM LAUNCHES AS CEO HOSTS LIVE CALL TODAY
source_name: Investing News Network / Contango Silver & Gold Inc. (NYSE:CTGO)
snippet: Contango Silver & Gold Inc. (NYSE:CTGO) confirmed June 22 that two helicopter-supported diamond drill rigs have mobilized to the Lucky Shot gold project in Alaska, launching the surface phase of a 29-hole / 6,800-metre planned program targeting infill of the Coleman zone and structural step-outs to test continuity between the Coleman and Lucky Shot vein systems — with CEO Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse and President Shawn Khunkhun holding a live investor webcast today (June 24) at 3:00 pm EST. The surface program follows a productive underground phase (6,020 metres completed) that returned multiple high-grade intercepts including 0.17 metres at 972.10 g/t gold in hole LSU26091, confirming the richness of the Lucky Shot vein system at depth; the next phase of underground drilling is scheduled for mid-August, making this 6,800-metre surface program the primary near-term catalyst ahead of what should be a dense fall drill release schedule at a project whose surface footprint remains vastly under-drilled relative to the historic mine's underground production history.

headline: CAULDRON +107% AS YANREY SEISMIC REVEALS CHANNEL LINKING TO PALADIN'S MANYINGEE — WA URANIUM BAN IS THE ONLY OBSTACLE
snippet: Cauldron Energy (ASX:CXU) surged over 107% for the week — closing at AU$0.120 from a prior-week close of AU$0.058 — after releasing results from a high-resolution passive seismic survey northeast of the Bennet Well deposit at its 100%-owned Yanrey uranium project in Western Australia that revealed a large, well-defined palaeochannel physically connecting the Manyingee North prospect to Paladin Energy's adjacent Manyingee uranium deposit and extending approximately six kilometres north from Cauldron's own ground; Bennet Well alone holds 30.9 million pounds of U3O8 in indicated and inferred resources, with total Yanrey resources at 55.6 million pounds. The discovery of a palaeochannel corridor linking the two deposits suggests the mineralizing system extends continuously between Manyingee and Bennet Well, potentially establishing a much larger roll-front uranium target than either deposit defines independently — the main structural barrier to Cauldron's stock fully repricing this resource is Western Australia's existing policy ban on uranium mining, a political constraint that investors will continue to weigh against Yanrey's resource quality as the WA government's periodic policy reviews approach.

headline: RECORD Q1 MARGINS, THEN THE SQUEEZE: FUEL COSTS SPIKE 50-100% AS IRAN CONFLICT GRINDS INTO SUMMER — OPEN-PIT MINERS MOST EXPOSED
snippet: Crux Investor's June 2026 analysis argues that while Q1 2026 delivered the gold mining sector's most profitable quarter on record — with gold averaging $4,873/oz against all-in sustaining costs well below $2,000/oz — Q2 presents a three-pronged margin compression: gold prices have softened approximately $200/oz from Q1 averages, refined fuel costs have increased 50-100% following the Iran conflict's impact on crude prices, and the insulating effect of on-site pre-shock fuel inventories that muted Q1 cost structures has now expired. The geographic exposure is sharply differentiated: underground, grid-connected operations see only 4-5% AISC impact from fuel spikes, while remote open-pit mines — particularly in Australia (91% fuel-import dependent), Chile, Peru, and the DRC — face 30-40% cost impacts that could significantly compress reported Q2 margins even as gold prices recover. For retail investors building junior mining positions, the analysis flags that ASX-listed remote open-pit developers and single-asset producers with high diesel dependency will report the weakest Q2 numbers relative to their AISC guidance, while Canadian underground producers benefit from both lower fuel exposure and stronger domestic copper/zinc credits.

headline: XXIX METAL OPTIONS PLUTO PROPERTY IN CHIBOUGAMAU — THIRD BLOCK ADDED TO OPEMISKA COPPER-GOLD DISTRICT FOOTPRINT
source_name: Junior Mining Network / XXIX Metal Corp. (TSXV:XXIX)
snippet: XXIX Metal Corp. (TSXV:XXIX) announced June 23 that it has entered into an option agreement with Germanium Mining Corp. to acquire a 100% interest in the Pluto Property in the Chapais-Chibougamau region of Quebec — contiguous to or proximal to the company's Opemiska copper-gold district holdings — adding a third block to a strategic district-scale consolidation in one of Quebec's historically significant copper belts. The Chibougamau camp hosts past-producing copper mines including the Copper Rand, Joe Mann, and Cedar Bay mines, all of which operated as high-grade underground operations exploiting volcanogenic massive sulphide and chalcopyrite-bornite replacement mineralisation; XXIX Metal's Opemiska consolidation strategy mirrors the acquisition approach that multiple major copper developers have used to build district-scale positions ahead of copper's structural demand growth from grid electrification, EV manufacturing, and AI data centre power infrastructure — sectors where copper demand is projected to grow faster than any new primary supply can realistically be brought to market before 2030.
